1:1.headline: 'Year three' of Jehoiakim clashes with Jeremiah's dates
1:1.body: Jeremiah says Nebuchadnezzar became king only in Jehoiakim's fourth year, so he could not attack in year three. Rashi and Metzudat David say it means year three of Jehoiakim's revolt against Babylon.

sources.quote: וּמַה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר בִּשְׁנַת שָׁלוֹשׁ? בִּשְׁנַת שָׁלוֹשׁ לְמִרְדּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the third year of Jehoiakim's rebellion, since Nebuchadnezzar became king only in Jehoiakim's fourth year.

sources.quote: ר״ל למרדו בנבוכדנצר למלוך מעצמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it counts from when Jehoiakim rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar to rule on his own.

1:2.headline: Shinar: where the Flood's dead were shaken out
1:2.body: Metzudat Zion says Shinar is Babylon. He reads the name from ננערו, 'were shaken out', because the dead of the Flood were shaken down there, it being the lowest land in the world.

sources.quote: שנער. היא בבל ע״ש שננערו בה מתי המבול כי היא עמוקה מכל העולם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Shinar is Babylon, named because the dead of the Flood were shaken out there, as it is the deepest land in the world.

1:3.headline: Saris: a eunuch, or simply a royal servant?
1:3.body: Ibn Ezra brings Rabbi Yehoshua: סריסים can mean eunuchs or just servants. He argues Daniel and his friends were not eunuchs, since Scripture never calls Daniel one.

sources.quote: כי מלת סריסים בלשון הקודש על שני טעמים: האחד: מסורסים. והשני: משרתים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Rabbi Yehoshua that the word sarisim has two senses in Hebrew: eunuchs and servants.

sources.quote: ולא תמצא בדניאל שהיה סריס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says you will not find that Daniel was a eunuch.

sources.quote: סריסיו. שריו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion explains 'his sarisim' as 'his officers'.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיָה שַׂר עַל מְשָׁרְתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the chief of the sarisim was in charge of the king's servants.

1:3.headline: A foreign word for nobles, found only here and in Esther
1:3.body: Rashi says the פרתמים were dukes. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion call it a foreign word, maybe Chaldean or Persian, known only from its context.

sources.quote: הַפַּרְתְּמִים. דּוּכָסִים
sources.says: Rashi says the partemim were dukes.

sources.quote: ומלת הפרתמים – זרה ולא תמצא במקרא רק במגלת אסתר, אולי הוא לשון כשדים או פרסיים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is foreign, found elsewhere only in Esther, perhaps Chaldean or Persian.

sources.quote: והיא מלה זרה ואולי היא מלשון כשדים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is a foreign word, perhaps Chaldean, and its sense is known only from context.

1:4.headline: Madda: knowledge you can explain, or an ordered science?
1:4.body: Ibn Ezra says מביני מדע are people who can put what they know into words for others. Malbim says מדע is an organized body of knowledge, like medicine, gathered from many people.

sources.quote: שיוכלו להבין לאחרים מה שיש בלבם ובמדעם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they could explain to others what was in their heart and mind.

sources.quote: וכלל המדע אשר התקבצה ע"י יודעים שונים ותהי לשטה כללית
sources.says: Malbim says madda is the whole body of knowledge gathered by many knowers into one system.

sources.quote: מדע. ענין מחשבה כמו גם במדעך מלך אל תקלל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says madda means thought, as in 'do not curse a king even in your thought'.

1:4.headline: 'Strength' to stand in the palace: holding back laughter and sleep
1:4.body: Rashi brings the sages: כח here is self-control. The youths could hold back from laughing, chatting, and sleeping out of awe for the king.

sources.quote: שֶׁיִּהְיוּ אוֹנְסִין עַצְמָן מִן הַשְּׂחוֹק וּמִן הַשִּׂיחָה וּמִן הַשֵּׁנָה מִפְּנֵי אֵימַת מַלְכוּת
sources.says: Rashi cites the sages that they could force themselves away from laughter, chatter and sleep out of fear of the king.

sources.quote: שתהיה תולדתם חזקה להסתיר העיטוש
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they needed a nature strong enough to hold back even a sneeze.

1:5.headline: Pat-bag: the king's food, named in a foreign tongue
1:5.body: Rashi says פת בג is the Chaldean name for the king's food, not bread, since pulses replaced it. Ibn Ezra thinks בג may be cooked meat, and Malbim reports a view that it was food offered to idols.

sources.quote: הוּא שֵׁם מַאֲכַל הַמֶּלֶךְ בִּלְשׁוֹן כַּשְׂדִּים
sources.says: Rashi says it is the name of the king's food in the Chaldean language.

sources.quote: וְאֵין זֵרְעוֹנִים חֲלִיפֵי לֶחֶם אֶלָּא חֲלִיפֵי תַבְשִׁיל
sources.says: Rashi rejects reading it as bread, since pulses replace cooked dishes, not bread.

sources.quote: אולי טעם בג הבשר המבושל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says bag means food, perhaps cooked meat.

sources.quote: יש מפרשים שפי' שם פת בג פת הנקרב לע"א
sources.says: Malbim reports that some explain pat-bag as food offered to idols.

1:5.headline: 'Some of them' or 'at the end of them'?
1:5.body: One reading: only some of the youths would go on to serve the king. Another reads it as time: at the end of the three years they would serve him.

sources.quote: יש אומרים: ומקצת הילדים ומקצת כלי בית האלהים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports a reading of 'some of the youths', like 'some of the vessels' in verse 2.

sources.quote: והוא שפירשו בסוף השנים הנזכרות, והנה כמוהו: ומקצת ימים עשרה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra also gives the reading 'at the end of the years', like 'at the end of ten days' later in the chapter.

sources.quote: מקצה שלשת השנים יעמדו בתמידות לפני המלך
sources.says: Metzudat David says at the end of the three years they would serve before the king.

sources.quote: שמקצת מן הילדים והם אלה שיצליחו בלמודם, יעמדו לפני המלך
sources.says: Malbim says some of the youths, those who did well in their studies, would serve before the king.

1:7.headline: Daniel renamed for a Babylonian god
1:7.body: Rashi says Belteshazzar is built on Bel, the god of Babylon, as the king himself says later. Malbim says only Daniel got his god's name, because the king saw something divine in him at once.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁל בָּבֶל שֶׁקְּרוּיָה בֵּל
sources.says: Rashi says the name is after the idol of Babylon called Bel.

sources.quote: בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר שֵׁם לְשׁוֹן חָכְמָה בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי
sources.says: Rashi adds that Belteshazzar is a name meaning wisdom in Aramaic.

sources.quote: שלדניאל נתן שם בלטשצר שהוא שם אלהי נבוכדנצר, כי הכיר מעלתו תיכף וראה בו ענין אלהי
sources.says: Malbim says Daniel was given the name of Nebuchadnezzar's god because the king saw his worth and something divine in him.

sources.quote: אולי המלה ההיא יורה בל׳ כשדים כמו דניאל בל׳ הקודש
sources.says: Metzudat David suggests the name may mean in Chaldean what Daniel means in Hebrew.

1:7.headline: Abed-nego: 'servant of Nebo' with one letter changed?
1:7.body: Azariah's new name means 'servant of Nego'. Ibn Ezra reports the Gaon's view that נגו is the same as נבו, Nebo, but says there is no proof.

sources.quote: והגאון אמר כי נגו כמו נבו אלא בלא ראיה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Gaon held that Nego is like Nebo, but without proof.

1:8.headline: Daniel would not 'soil himself' with the king's food
1:8.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion say יתגאל means to dirty oneself, as in לחם מגואל, 'defiled bread'. Malbim says Daniel used this blunt word to the officer, at great risk, instead of making an excuse.

sources.quote: יִתְגָּאַל. לְשׁוֹן לִכְלוּךְ
sources.says: Rashi says the word means getting dirty.

sources.quote: יתגאל. ענין לכלוך וטנוף כמו לחם מגואל
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means dirt and filth, as in 'defiled bread' in Malachi.

sources.quote: לא אמר לו אמתלאות וטעמים אחרים, רק אמר בפירוש אשר לא יתגאל
sources.says: Malbim says Daniel gave no excuses or other reasons, but said plainly that he would not defile himself.

1:10.headline: Faces 'raging': the word for anger used for looking unwell
1:10.body: The officer fears the king will see their faces זועפים. Metzudat Zion says the word comes from rage, because an angry face changes for the worse.

sources.quote: ר״ל רעים והוא מל׳ זעף וכעס כי הכועס נשתנה מראית פניו לרוע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means poor-looking, from the word for rage, since an angry man's face changes for the worse.

sources.quote: כפני אנשים זועפים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says their faces would look like the faces of angry men.

1:10.headline: 'You will make my head a debt to the king'
1:10.body: Rashi says the officer means he would be liable to have his head cut off. Ibn Ezra ties וחיבתם to חוב, debt, as in חבולתו חוב, 'his pledge for a debt'.

sources.quote: תִּגְרְמוּ לִי לְהִתְחַיֵּב לְהַתִּיז רֹאשִׁי
sources.says: Rashi says they would cause him to be liable to have his head cut off.

sources.quote: וחיבתם - מגזרת חבולתו חוב
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word comes from the root of 'his pledge for a debt' (chov).

1:12.headline: Why a test of exactly ten days?
1:12.body: Ibn Ezra says scholars of nature held that a living body can bear harm for only nine days. Malbim cites doctors: bad food shows its harm on the face within ten days.

sources.quote: כי אין יכולת בחי לסבול הרעה, רק ט' ימים ככה הזכירו בעלי התולדות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says a living thing can bear harm only nine days, as students of nature taught.

sources.quote: שהמזונות הרעים יוכר היזקם בהזנת האדם עד עשרה ימים
sources.says: Malbim cites the doctors that the harm of bad food shows within ten days.

1:15.headline: Fatter on beans: a miracle, or just good food?
1:15.body: Metzudat Zion says בריאי here means plump, as with fat Eglon. Malbim calls it beyond nature, but Ibn Ezra rejects the Gaon's 'great miracle' and credits the rice they ate.

sources.quote: ובריאי. ענין שומן כמו ועגלון איש בריא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means fatness, as in 'Eglon was a fat man'.

sources.quote: שזה חוץ לטבע כי הזרעונים לא ישמינו את הגוף כבשר ויין
sources.says: Malbim says this was beyond nature, since pulses do not fatten the body like meat and wine.

sources.quote: ויאמר הגאון: זה היה נס גדול ואין צורך כי היו אוכלים אורז
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reports the Gaon called it a great miracle, and replies there is no need, since they ate rice.

1:20.headline: 'Ten hands' better: hands meaning shares
1:20.body: Metzudat Zion says ידות here means parts, as in 'four parts' in Genesis 47. Ibn Ezra adds that ten may simply mean 'many'.

sources.quote: ידות. חלקים כמו וארבע הידות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says yadot means parts, as in 'and four parts'.

sources.quote: ויתכן היות עשר לשון רבים כמו מעשרה שליטים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'ten' may be a way of saying many, as in 'more than ten rulers'.

1:20.headline: Chartumim: those who seek answers from dead men's bones
1:20.body: Rashi says they consulted טימי מתים, the bones of the dead, using the Aramaic word טמיא for bones. Metzudat Zion says instead that they were scholars of nature.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ שֶׁשּׁוֹאֲלִים בְּטִימֵי מֵתִים, בְּעַצְמוֹת מֵתִים
sources.says: Rashi says these are the ones who inquire by the bones of the dead.

sources.quote: החרטומים. הם חכמי הטבע
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the chartumim were scholars of nature.

1:20.headline: Ashafim: men who pressed the stars, or doctors?
1:20.body: Rashi, following the Tanchuma, says they pressed the stars for answers. Metzudat Zion says they were doctors.

sources.quote: אֵלּוּ שֶׁדּוֹחֲקִים בַּמַּזָּל
sources.says: Rashi says these are the ones who press the constellations, as the Tanchuma explains.

sources.quote: האשפים. הם חכמי הרפואה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the ashafim were experts in medicine.

1:21.headline: 'Until year one of Cyrus', not until a full year
1:21.body: Ibn Ezra notes the verse says שנת אחת and not שנה אחת. He reads it as some time within that year, not after a whole year had passed.

sources.quote: ואילו היה כתוב עד שנה אחת, היה נראה כי שנה שלימה עברה ובאומרו שנת אחת, הטעם בתוך השנה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says 'shanah achat' would mean a full year passed, but 'shenat achat' means within the year.

10:1.headline: צבא גדול: a great host of angels, or a long time to come
10:1.body: Metzudat David reads a great host of angels shown to Daniel. Rashi reads צבא as a span of time: the vision will come true only after a long time. Ibn Ezra cites a reading from Job 7:1, "man's term of service on earth".

sources.quote: גם נגלה אליו צבא גדול של מלאכי מעלה
sources.says: Metzudat David says a great host of heavenly angels was also shown to him.

sources.quote: וְצָבָא גָדוֹל. וּלִזְמַן אָרוֹךְ יָבֹא
sources.says: Rashi says it means the vision will come after a long time.

sources.quote: ור' משה בן בלעם אמר: שהוא כמו צבא לאנוש עלי ארץ
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites Moshe ben Bil'am, who compares "man has a term of service on earth".

sources.quote: אמר הגאון: כי וצבא גדול כמו ודי הוה צבה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites the Gaon, who reads it like the Aramaic צבה, "what he wished".

10:6.headline: כתרשיש: the color of a bluish gem, or as wide as the sea
10:6.body: Metzudat David reads תרשיש as a gem with a bluish look. Rashi brings the Rabbis, who read it as the sea of Tarshish: the angel's body was as vast as that sea. Maimonides cites this to say an angel in a prophetic vision is a third of the world wide.

sources.quote: גופו היה כעין אבן תרשיש הנוטה למראה התכלת
sources.says: Metzudat David says his body looked like the tarshish stone, which leans toward blue.

sources.quote: גּוּפוֹ גָּדוֹל שְׁנֵי אֲלָפִים פַּרְסָה כְּמִדַּת יָם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ תַרְשִׁישׁ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Rabbis: his body was two thousand parsa, the size of the sea named Tarshish.

sources.quote: כי רוחב מלאך אחד במראה הנבואה הוא כמידת שליש עולם, על פי מה שנאמר
sources.says: Maimonides says the width of one angel in a prophetic vision is a third of the world, based on this verse.

10:7.headline: The men who fled were the prophets Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi
10:7.body: Rashi cites the Rabbis: the men with Daniel were the prophets Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi. They did not see the vision but felt dread, because, Rashi says, a person's star in heaven sees what he cannot.

sources.quote: אָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה הֵם חַגַּי זְכַרְיָה וּמַלְאָכִי
sources.says: Rashi says the Rabbis identified them as Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi.

sources.quote: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָדָם אֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא נִבְעָת מִמֶּנּוּ, מַזָּלוֹ שֶׁבָּרָקִיעַ רוֹאֵהוּ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Rabbis: even when a person does not see what frightens him, his star in heaven sees it.

sources.quote: שלכן הרגישו בדבר ונפל עליהם חרדה כי היו נביאים
sources.says: Malbim says they sensed something and were seized by dread because they were prophets.

10:11.headline: איש חמדות: a pure man, or a man of fine qualities
10:11.body: Rashi reads it as "a pure man", as he read חמדות as "clean" bread in verse 3. Metzudat David reads it as a man with many desirable virtues.

sources.quote: אִישׁ חֲמֻדוֹת. אִישׁ טָהוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says איש חמדות means a pure man.

sources.quote: איש חמודות. בעל מעלות חמודות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means a man of desirable virtues.

10:12.headline: "I came because of your words": Daniel let the angel back in
10:12.body: Plainly, the angel came on this errand because of Daniel's prayer. Rashi brings the Rabbis' reading in Yoma: the angel had been sent out from behind the heavenly curtain, and Daniel's words brought him back in.

sources.quote: בָּאתִי בִּשְׁלִיחוּת זוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל דְּבָרֶיךָ
sources.says: Rashi says the angel came on this mission because of Daniel's words.

sources.quote: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ דָּרְשׁוּ בְּמַסֶּכֶת יוֹמָא: וַאֲנִי בָאתִי לְתוֹךְ הַפַּרְגּוֹד עַל יָדְךָ, שֶׁהָיִיתִי מְגֹרָשׁ מִתּוֹכוֹ
sources.says: Rashi cites the Rabbis in Yoma: I came back inside the curtain through you, after being driven out.

10:13.headline: נותרתי: "I was left there alone", or "I gained the upper hand"
10:13.body: Metzudat David reads it as being left alone to fight the prince of Persia. Malbim reads it from יתרון, "advantage": with Michael's help the angel gained the upper hand over Persia's kings.

sources.quote: נותרתי אני לבדי להלחם בו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the angel was left alone to fight him.

sources.quote: וַאֲנִי נוֹתַרְתִּי שָׁם. לְשַׁתֵּק אֶת שַׂר פָּרַס שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the angel stayed there to silence the prince of Persia in heaven.

sources.quote: וע"י מיכאל נותרתי ניתן לי היתרון
sources.says: Malbim says that through Michael the angel was given the advantage.

10:14.headline: "What will happen": chance is only a human way of speaking
10:14.body: The verb comes from the same root as מקרה, "chance". Metzudat David says the angel speaks the way people do, calling something chance when they do not know its cause. In truth nothing happens by chance.

sources.quote: אמר בל׳ בני אדם החושבים למקרה דבר שלא ידעו סבתו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the angel speaks in human language, as people call a thing chance when they do not know its cause.

sources.quote: אולם אין מקרה בעולם הכל נעשה בגזרה
sources.says: Metzudat David says there is no chance in the world; everything happens by decree.

10:16.headline: צירי: Daniel's joints slipped like a door off its hinges
10:16.body: ציר is the hinge a door turns on. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say the word was borrowed for the body's joints, which turn in their sockets. From fear, Daniel felt them slip out of place.

sources.quote: וְסוֹבֵב בְּתוֹכָם כְּדֶלֶת עַל צִירָהּ בְּחוֹר הַמִּפְתָּן
sources.says: Rashi says each joint turns in its socket like a door on its hinge.

sources.quote: צִירַי נֶהֶפְכוּ לְהִשָּׁמֵט מִמְּקוֹמָם מֵרוֹב רֶתֶת וַחֲרָדָה
sources.says: Rashi says his joints turned to slip out of place from great trembling and fear.

sources.quote: כל דבר התקוע זה בזה נקרא ציר והוא מושאל מן צירי הדלתות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says anything set into something else is called ציר, a word borrowed from door hinges.

11:6.headline: בעתים: "in times of trouble", or astrologers who know the times?
11:6.body: Rashi reads it as the one who supports her in every time of her distress. Metzudat David and Ibn Ezra read it as the astrologers with her, who told her the times from the stars.

sources.quote: וּמַחֲזִיקָהּ בְּכָל עֵת צָרָתָהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the one who supports her in every time of her trouble.

sources.quote: הם אצטגנינים המחזיקים אותה בהודעת פעולת העתים לפי מהלך הכוכבים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are astrologers who support her by telling her what the times will bring, by the movement of the stars.

sources.quote: וחכמי המזלות שהיו עמה, וזהו: ומחזיקה בעתים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the astrologers who were with her.

11:6.headline: הילדה: her father, or the one who raised her?
11:6.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say it means her father, who fathered her. Malbim says it means the person who raised her like a father, and compares אשר ילדה לעדריאל.

sources.quote: הִיא וּמְבִיאֶיהָ וְהַיֹּלְדָהּ. הוּא אָבִיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says והילדה means her father.

sources.quote: והיולדה. הוא אביה מלך הנגב
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is her father, the king of the south.

sources.quote: והיולדה היינו האומן והמגדל אותה, (שהיה לה כאב, כמ"ש אשר ילדה לעדריאל)
sources.says: Malbim says it means the one who fostered and raised her, who was like a father to her, as in אשר ילדה לעדריאל.

11:7.headline: מנצר means "a branch from", and the מ means "one of"
11:7.body: This is a rare word. Metzudat Zion says it means a branch, as in ונצר משרשיו יפרה. Ibn Ezra says the מ stands for "one of": one of the sons of the king of Egypt.

sources.quote: ענין ענף כמו ונצר משרשיו יפרה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a branch, as in ונצר משרשיו יפרה.

sources.quote: שרשי זאת הבת והמ"ם ישמש בעבור אחד מן בניו של מלך מצרים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the roots are this daughter's, and the מ is used for "one of" the sons of the king of Egypt.

11:12.headline: ונשא: lifted up in pride, or carried off?
11:12.body: Rashi says the crowd became very proud. Metzudat Zion says ונשא means taking. Metzudat David says the king of the south takes the crowd for himself and carries them off captive, and so his heart grows proud.

sources.quote: שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ צָפוֹן לְהִתְגָּאוֹת מְאֹד
sources.says: Rashi says the crowd of the king of the north grew very proud.

sources.quote: ונשא. ענין לקיחה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ונשא means taking.

sources.quote: מלך הנגב ישא ההמון לעצמו ויביאה בשבי ובזה ירום לבבו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the king of the south will take the crowd for himself and bring them captive, and so his heart will be lifted up.

11:14.headline: פריצי: lawbreakers who break through the fence
11:14.body: Metzudat Zion says it means wicked men who break through the fence of truth and justice. Metzudat David says it means the wicked of Israel. Rashi passes on Rav Saadia's view that it means the lawless of Israel and their party.

sources.quote: פריצי. רשעים הפורצים גדר האמת והצדק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means wicked men who break through the fence of truth and justice.

sources.quote: ובני פריצי עמך. ר״ל רשעי ישראל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means the wicked of Israel.

sources.quote: רָאִיתִי בְּשֵׁם רַב סְעַדְיָה שֶׁזּוֹ פְּרִיצֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְסִיעָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says he saw in the name of Rav Saadia that this means the lawless of Israel and their party.

11:16.headline: וכלה: he destroyed the land, or it was all in his hand?
11:16.body: Rashi says he destroyed the land with his armies. Malbim says the conquest was finished, and the whole land was in his hand.

sources.quote: וְכִלָּה אֶת הָאָרֶץ בְּאוּכְלוּסָיו
sources.says: Rashi says he destroyed the land with his armies.

sources.quote: וכלה בידו, ואז גמר הכיבוש הזה מארץ סוריא וכל הארץ היתה כולה בידו וברשותו
sources.says: Malbim says that then he finished this conquest of Syria, and the whole land was entirely in his hand and power.

11:17.headline: בתקף: the strength of the south's kingdom, or of his own?
11:17.body: Rashi says the northern king comes against the strength of the whole kingdom of the south. Malbim agrees: it means Egypt itself, where the south's strength lies. Metzudat David says he comes with strength, bringing a great people from all his own kingdom.

sources.quote: לָבוֹא בְּתֹקֶף כָּל מַלְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַנֶּגֶב
sources.says: Rashi says he comes to the strength of the whole kingdom of the king of the south.

sources.quote: לכבוש את ארץ מצרים עצמה ששם תוקף מלכות מלך הנגב
sources.says: Malbim says he goes to conquer Egypt itself, where the strength of the south's kingdom is.

sources.quote: ישים מחשבתו לבוא בא"י בחוזק עם רב מכל אנשי מלכותו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he sets his mind to come into the land of Israel with strength, with a large people from all the men of his kingdom.

11:17.headline: בת הנשים: Israel, the queen of Sheba, or his own daughter?
11:17.body: Rashi says the "daughter of women" is the congregation of Israel, the fairest of women. Ibn Ezra says it is the queen of Sheba. Malbim says it is a daughter of the king, born to one of his wives.

sources.quote: זוֹ כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל ״הַיָּפָה בַּנָּשִׁים״ (שיר השירים א:ח)
sources.says: Rashi says this is the congregation of Israel, "the fairest of women" in Song of Songs.

sources.quote: ובת הנשים - היא מלכת שבא יתן לו מלך הנגב להשחיתה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is the queen of Sheba, whom the king of the south will give him to ruin.

sources.quote: בת הנשים בת א' שהיה לו מנשיו
sources.says: Malbim says it is a daughter of one of the wives he had.

11:20.headline: מעביר נוגש: removes the oppressor, or goes round collecting tax?
11:20.body: Rashi says it is Mattathias, who removes the Greek oppressor from Israel. Malbim says the king did nothing but pass through the cities collecting the tax owed to Rome.

sources.quote: מַתִּתְיָהוּ בֶּן יוֹחָנָן הַמַּעֲבִיר נוֹגֵשׂ יָוָן מֵעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says Mattathias son of Yochanan removes the Greek oppressor from Israel.

sources.quote: רק מה שעבר בערים לנגוש המס שהיה צריך לתת להרומיים בכל שנה, וע"ז קראו מעביר נוגש הדר מלכות
sources.says: Malbim says he only passed through the cities to collect the tax he had to give Rome each year, and so it is called מעביר נוגש הדר מלכות.

11:21.headline: חלקלקות: smooth flattery, or darkness?
11:21.body: Metzudat Zion says it comes from חלק, smooth: flattery and soft words. Malbim agrees: he won the kingdom by flattery and smooth words. Ibn Ezra reads it differently: "in darkness, without counsel".

sources.quote: בחלקלקות. מלשון חלק ר״ל חניפה ודברים רכים וחלקים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is from חלק, smooth, meaning flattery and soft, smooth words.

sources.quote: כמבואר בדה"י שע"י חנופה ודברי חלק פעל
sources.says: Malbim says as the histories explain, he worked through flattery and smooth words.

sources.quote: בחלקלקות - במחשך בלי עצה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means in the dark, without counsel.

11:24.headline: יבזור means to scatter, with ב standing in for פ
11:24.body: This is a rare word. Rashi says it means יפזר, he will scatter, and compares בזר עמים in Psalms. Metzudat Zion says the same, and adds that the lip letters ב, ו, מ and פ swap with one another.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ יְפַזֵּר, וְכֵן ״בִּזַּר עַמִּים״ (תהלים סח:לא)
sources.says: Rashi says it is like יפזר, as in בזר עמים in Psalms.

sources.quote: יפזר וכן בזר עמים (תהלים סח) כי בומ"ף מתחלף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means יפזר, as in בזר עמים, because the letters ב, ו, מ and פ swap.

11:30.headline: ציים: ships, or groups of people?
11:30.body: Metzudat Zion and Ibn Ezra say ציים are ships. Rashi says they are סיעות, groups or parties.

sources.quote: צִיִּים. סִיעוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says ציים means groups.

sources.quote: ציים. אניות כמו וצי אדיר
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ציים means ships, as in וצי אדיר.

sources.quote: ציים - הם האניות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ציים are the ships.

11:31.headline: משומם: the idol is struck dumb, like a silent stone
11:31.body: Metzudat David says the idol set up in the Temple is called משומם because it is mute and silent, like a lifeless stone.

sources.quote: יעמדו צורת עכו"ם המשוקץ הנאלם ומושתק כאבן דומם
sources.says: Metzudat David says they will set up the image of the abominable idol, which is mute and silenced like a dumb stone.

11:34.headline: ונלוו: they join the enemy, or join the faithful?
11:34.body: Metzudat David says many Jews left the faith to join the enemy, drawn by smooth words. Ibn Ezra says they joined with the believers. Metzudat Zion says the word means joining together.

sources.quote: אבל רבים מישראל יצאו מן הדת להתחבר עליהם בעבור חלקלקות אמריהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says many of Israel left the faith to join them because of their smooth words.

sources.quote: ונלוו עליהם - עם המאמינים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ונלוו עליהם means with the believers.

sources.quote: ונלוו. ענין התחברות כמו הפעם ילוה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means joining, as in הפעם ילוה.

11:36.headline: על כל אל: against every god, or over every power?
11:36.body: Malbim reads it as every god: the king abolishes the worship of idols. Metzudat David and Metzudat Zion say אל here means strength and power, so he raises himself over every mighty one.

sources.quote: ויתגדל על כל אל, שיבטל עבודת האלילים שעבדו קודם לכן
sources.says: Malbim says he will exalt himself over every god, in that he abolishes the idol worship they served before.

sources.quote: על כל אל. על כל חוזק ובעל כח
sources.says: Metzudat David says על כל אל means over every strength and every powerful one.

sources.quote: אל. ענין אומץ וחוזק כמו יש לאל ידי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says אל means courage and strength, as in יש לאל ידי.

11:37.headline: אלהי אבותיו: the LORD, or the planet his fathers served?
11:37.body: Rashi says the God of his fathers is the Holy One, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel. Metzudat David and Malbim say it is the star his fathers served: Metzudat David names צדק, and Malbim names צדק and נוגה.

sources.quote: לֹא יִתֵּן לֵב לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁהוּא אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אֲבוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi says he will not give heed to the Holy One, who is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, his fathers.

sources.quote: לא יתן לב להתבונן לעבוד את אלהי אבותיו אשר עבדו מאז לכוכב צדק
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will not think to serve the god of his fathers, whom they served from of old, the star צדק.

sources.quote: שאבותיו היו עובדים לצדק ונוגה
sources.says: Malbim says his fathers used to serve צדק and נוגה.

11:37.headline: חמדת נשים: Israel, "the fairest of women"?
11:37.body: Rashi and Metzudat David read "the desire of women" as Israel, called the fairest of women in Song of Songs. Ibn Ezra argues against a scholar who explained "women" as cities, calling that closer to drash than to the plain meaning.

sources.quote: חֶמְדַּת נָשִׁים. כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַיָּפָה בַּנָּשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says חמדת נשים is the congregation of Israel, the fairest of women.

sources.quote: לא יבין על מעלת ישראל הנקראת היפה בנשים
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will not regard the worth of Israel, who is called the fairest of women.

sources.quote: וכל חמדת נשים לא יבין וזה היה אוהב נשים ופירש נשים מדינות, וזה קרוב אל דרש ואיננו פשט
sources.says: Ibn Ezra objects that this king loved women, and that explaining "women" as cities is close to drash and not the plain meaning.

11:40.headline: וישתער: from the word for a storm, with ש for ס
11:40.body: Metzudat Zion says it is the same as ויסתער spelled with a samekh, from סערה, a storm wind. Metzudat David reads it as fighting like a storm wind. Ibn Ezra compares בסופה ובסערה.

sources.quote: וישתער. כמו ויסתער בסמ"ך והוא מלשון רוח סערה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is like ויסתער with a samekh, and comes from the language of a storm wind.

sources.quote: ילחם בו כמו רוח סערה
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will fight against him like a storm wind.

sources.quote: כמו: בסופה ובסערה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra compares it to בסופה ובסערה.

11:43.headline: במצעדיו: trampled under his steps, or following behind him?
11:43.body: Metzudat David says Libya and Cush will be trampled under the soles of his feet. Ibn Ezra says they are close to Egypt and will walk in his steps, coming under his rule.

sources.quote: יהיו רמוסים במצעדי כפות רגליו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they will be trampled under the steps of the soles of his feet.

sources.quote: הם סמוכים למצרים יהיו במצעדיו של מלך צפון, שיסורו אל משמעתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says they are next to Egypt and will be at the steps of the king of the north, turning to his authority.

11:43.headline: במכמני: hidden treasures, tied to an Aramaic word and maybe to coins
11:43.body: This word is used only here. Metzudat Zion says it means hidden stores, and points to the Aramaic ודלא כמן, from the Targum on Exodus 21. Ibn Ezra cites the same Aramaic and guesses it may come from דרכמונים, a kind of coin.

sources.quote: עניינו אוצרות מסתרי׳ ודומה לו בל׳ ארמית כי ואשר לא צדה (שמות כא) ת״א ודלא כמן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means hidden treasures, like the Aramaic in the Targum of ואשר לא צדה, ודלא כמן.

sources.quote: ומשל במכמני - תרגום ואשר לא צדה ודלא כמן ליה אולי הוא מגזרת דרכמונים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites the Targum of ואשר לא צדה, and says perhaps it comes from the root of דרכמונים.

11:45.headline: אפדנו: a palace, a rare word known from the Talmud
11:45.body: Metzudat Zion says it means a palace, and cites חזאי אפדנא דאביי in the Talmud. Metzudat David says it means the tents of his palace.

sources.quote: עניינו ארמון ובדרז״ל חזאי אפדנא דאביי דנפל (ברכות נח)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a palace, and the sages say חזאי אפדנא דאביי דנפל.

sources.quote: יעמיד אהלי ארמונו בין הימים
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will set the tents of his palace between the seas.

2:1.headline: 'Year two' of his reign cannot mean what it seems
2:1.body: Daniel and his friends were still in three years of training, so year two of the king's reign looks too early. Rashi counts from the Temple's destruction instead. Ibn Ezra counts from when the king ruled all nations.

sources.quote: אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi says it cannot mean the second year of his reign, but the second year after he destroyed the Temple, as taught in Seder Olam.

sources.quote: והם לא השלימו עדיין חק למודם
sources.says: Malbim asks how Daniel could be in danger in year two when he and his friends had not yet finished their training.

sources.quote: והנכון בעיני: למלכותו על כל הגוים שהזכיר ירמיה שיכבשם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra holds it means the second year of his rule over all the nations that Jeremiah said he would conquer.

2:1.headline: A doubled verb for a doubled worry
2:1.body: Of Pharaoh the Torah says ותפעם, his spirit was troubled. Here the verb has an extra letter, ותתפעם. Rashi says the doubling fits a king who lost both the dream and its meaning.

sources.quote: וְכָאן שֶׁנֶּעְלַם מִמֶּנּוּ גַּם הַחֲלוֹם נִכְפְּלָה הַלָּשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says Pharaoh forgot only the meaning, but this king forgot the dream too, so the word is doubled.

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם שְׁתֵּי פְעִימוֹת, שִׁכְחַת הַחֲלוֹם וְהַעֲלָמַת פִּתְרוֹנוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says there were two blows here: he forgot the dream and its meaning was hidden.

sources.quote: א"כ מה יעשה כי הוא אומר ותפעם רוחי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra brings this reading from the Gaon, then objects that the king himself uses the short form in verse 3.

2:1.headline: Was his sleep broken, or did it hold him?
2:1.body: Rashi reads נהיתה as broken: the king could not sleep again. Malbim reads it as 'came over him': he stayed asleep through a frightening dream, which showed it was a true dream.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן שִׁבָּרוֹן, כְּמוֹ ״הוֹוָה עַל הוֹוָה״
sources.says: Rashi says the word means breaking, as in Ezekiel's 'disaster upon disaster'.

sources.quote: ר"ל שאחרי החלום נשאר ישן ולא הקיץ משנתו
sources.says: Malbim says it means that after the dream he stayed asleep and did not wake.

2:2.headline: Who were the אשפים: doctors or stargazers?
2:2.body: The king calls the אשפים along with his magicians. Ibn Ezra says they were doctors, who read the body because dreams follow the body. Malbim says they were astrologers.

sources.quote: גם קרא לאשפים שהם יודעים בדפק הזרוע או במי השתן השתנות הגוף ורובי החלומות הולכים על מתכונת הגוף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the אשפים read the pulse and urine, and were called because most dreams follow the state of the body.

sources.quote: שהם האצטגנינים חוזי בכוכבים
sources.says: Malbim says the אשפים were astrologers who read the stars.

sources.quote: וְאָשַׁף. הַדּוֹחֵק בַּמַּזָּל
sources.says: Rashi says the אשף is one who presses on fortune.

2:8.headline: Buying time, or already sold to death?
2:8.body: זבנין means buying or selling. Ibn Ezra and Malbim read it as 'you are buying time', stalling. Rashi reads it as 'at this hour you are handed over to death'.

sources.quote: אֲשֶׁר זוֹ הַשָּׁעָה אַתֶּם מְסוּרִים לַמָּוֶת
sources.says: Rashi says it means that at this hour they are handed over to death.

sources.quote: אשר בעת הזאת אתם נמכרים ונמסרים למיתה
sources.says: Metzudat David says they are being sold and handed over to death.

sources.quote: באמת יודע אני כי העת אתם קונים, והטעם אתם דוחים את השעה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'you are buying time', putting off the moment.

2:11.headline: 'No one else' can tell it, or 'Aaron is not here'?
2:11.body: The wise men say ואחרן לא איתי, no one else can tell the dream. The midrash hears ואהרן, Aaron: the high priest who could ask God is gone. The king then blames them for urging him to destroy the Temple.

sources.quote: כֹּהֵן הַלּוֹבֵשׁ אוּרִים וְתֻמִּים אֵינוֹ כָאן שֶׁיַּגִּיד לְךָ
sources.says: Rashi brings Midrash Tanchuma: the priest who wears the Urim and Tummim is not here to tell you, and the king grew angry that they had advised him to destroy the Temple.

sources.quote: ואהרן לא יש שישאל באורים ותומים
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages that the wise men meant Aaron is not here to ask through the Urim and Tummim.

2:11.headline: Gods, or angels?
2:11.body: The wise men say only אלהין, who do not live among people, could tell the dream. The word often means gods, but Rashi reads it as angels. Ibn Ezra uses this verse to show the word can name any holy being without a body.

sources.quote: אַךְ הַמַּלְאָכִים אֲשֶׁר מְדוֹרָם עִם בָּשָׂר וָדָם אֵינֶנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means the angels, whose dwelling is not with flesh and blood.

sources.quote: והוא כולל כל קדוש שאינו גוף, ולא כח בגוף
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word is a title covering every holy being that has no body, and cites this verse.

2:14.headline: The word for 'counsel' behind 'by the serpent's counsel'
2:14.body: עטא means counsel or advice. Rashi on the Talmud uses this verse to explain the saying that people die בעטיו של נחש, through the serpent's counsel in Eden.

sources.quote: הֵשִׁיב עֵצָה וְטַעַם לְאַרְיוֹךְ
sources.says: Rashi says Daniel answered Arioch with counsel and reason.

sources.quote: בעצתו של נחש שהשיא לחוה
sources.says: Rashi explains 'by the serpent's עטיו' as by the serpent's counsel to Eve, citing this word in Daniel.

2:14.headline: Chief of the slaughterers, or of the cooks?
2:14.body: טבח can mean killing or cooking. Ibn Ezra says Potiphar's title in Genesis meant chief cook, but here Arioch is chief executioner, because he went out to kill.

sources.quote: כי מלת טבח בלשון הקדש תתפרש לשני טעמים: האחד: הריגה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says טבח has two senses, killing and cooking, and here it is killing because Arioch went out to kill.

sources.quote: שַׂר הַהוֹרְגִים הַמְחֻיָּבִים הֲרִיגָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means the officer who executes those sentenced to death.

2:15.headline: Why is the decree so harsh, or so hasty?
2:15.body: Daniel asks why the decree is מהחצפה. Rashi reads it as brazen or harsh. Ibn Ezra and Metzudat Zion read it as hurried, since a brazen person rushes to shame others.

sources.quote: מָה זֶּה שֶׁדַּת הַמֶּלֶךְ חֲצוּפָה לַהֲרוֹג
sources.says: Rashi says Daniel asked why the king's decree to kill is so brazen.

sources.quote: טעם מהחצפה מהירות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means speed.

sources.quote: ממהרת והוא מל׳ חצוף הממהר להביש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means hasty, from the brazen person who is quick to shame others.

2:23.headline: Daniel switches from 'me' to 'us'
2:23.body: Daniel thanks God, who 'made known to me' and then 'made known to us'. Ibn Ezra and Malbim say only Daniel received the secret, but his friends had prayed for it with him.

sources.quote: כאומר: לא בזכותי לבדי הודעתני זה הסוד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Daniel meant that the secret was not revealed through his own merit alone.

sources.quote: ואמר הודעתני בלשון יחיד, ובעינא והודעתנא בלשון רבים
sources.says: Malbim notes the switch from singular to plural: Daniel and his friends asked, but God told only Daniel.

2:27.headline: The גזרין: diviners who 'cut' a verdict on the future
2:27.body: גזרין is a kind of diviner. Ibn Ezra links the name to cutting: they decide the future as if it were certain.

sources.quote: פירושו חותכי משפט האומרים כי כן יהיה בלא ספק וכן גוזרין
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says diviners 'cut a verdict', saying it will surely happen, and that גוזרין means the same.

sources.quote: שֵׁם מִין בַּעַל כִּשּׁוּף
sources.says: Rashi says it is the name of a kind of sorcerer.

sources.quote: הם בעלי הקסם ההולכים לקראת נחשים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are diviners who go out to look for omens.

2:28.headline: The wise men said 'gods'; Daniel says 'one God'
2:28.body: The wise men said only אלהין, gods, could tell the dream. Daniel answers with אלה in the singular: there is a God in heaven. Ibn Ezra points out the contrast.

sources.quote: החכמים אמרו לו: אלהין ודניאל אמר אלה חד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra notes that the wise men said gods, and Daniel said one God.

2:31.headline: 'This statue', or 'a statue with a great base'?
2:31.body: Most read דכן as 'this'. Malbim adds that the statue appeared again before the king's eyes as Daniel spoke. Rashi instead splits the word: a statue whose כן, base, was great.

sources.quote: צֶלֶם אֲשֶׁר הָיָה לוֹ כַּן גָּדוֹל
sources.says: Rashi says it was a statue that had a large base.

sources.quote: צלמא דכן - צלם זה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means 'this statue'.

sources.quote: באותו רגע נצטייר המחזה שנית לפני נבוכדנצר
sources.says: Malbim says that as Daniel began to speak, the vision appeared again before Nebuchadnezzar, so Daniel could say 'this one'.

2:36.headline: Why does Daniel say 'we will tell'?
2:36.body: Daniel says 'we will tell its meaning', though he speaks alone. Ibn Ezra says it is modesty: 'I and wisdom'. He rejects the idea that Daniel used a royal 'we' before the king of kings.

sources.quote: ופתרונו אוכל אני והחכמה לפתור אותו, על כן לשון רבים וזה דרך מוסר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Daniel used the plural out of politeness, meaning he and wisdom together can interpret it.

sources.quote: ואיך ידבר דניאל בלשון גדולה עם נבוכדנצר שהיה מלך מלכים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says Daniel would never speak in a grand royal plural to Nebuchadnezzar, the king of kings.

2:37.headline: 'King of kings': the king, or God?
2:37.body: Daniel seems to call Nebuchadnezzar king of kings. Rashi brings the sages: everywhere else in Daniel the phrase means a human king, but here it means God, who gave the king his kingdom.

sources.quote: כָּל מֶלֶךְ מַלְכַיָּא דְּדָנִיֵּאל מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם, חוּץ מִזֶּה
sources.says: Rashi says, following the sages, that every 'king of kings' in Daniel is a human king except this one, which refers to God.

sources.quote: ור"ל מלך שהמליך אותו מלך המלכים יתברך
sources.says: Malbim says it means a king whom the King of kings made king.

2:39.headline: 'Lower than you' uses the word for the ground
2:39.body: The next kingdom will be ארע, lower than Babylon, as silver is below gold. Ibn Ezra notes that this is why the earth is called ארעא in Aramaic: it is below everything.

sources.quote: ובעבורה נקראה הארץ ארעא, כי היא למטה מהכל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ארע means low, and that this is why the earth is called ארעא, since it is lowest of all.

sources.quote: תַּחְתּוֹנָה וּנְמוּכָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהַכֶּסֶף נָמוּךְ וְשָׁפָל מֵהַזָּהָב
sources.says: Rashi says it means lower, as silver is lower than gold.

3:1.headline: Sixty cubits tall and six wide: how did it stand?
3:1.body: A statue sixty cubits high but only six wide would topple. Rashi brings Rav Bivi: it kept falling until they poured all of Jerusalem's gold at its feet.

sources.quote: מַעֲמִידִין אוֹתוֹ וְנוֹפֵל, עַד שֶׁהֵבִיאוּ כָּל זָהָב שֶׁל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
sources.says: Rashi asks how a statue six cubits thick could stand sixty high, and brings Rav Bivi: it kept falling until all of Jerusalem's gold was poured at its feet.

3:1.headline: The plain of Dura: where the Tower of Babel was built
3:1.body: Malbim brings the sages that the plain of Dura is the same valley where the builders of the Tower of Babel gathered. Both tried to build a kingdom that would defy heaven.

sources.quote: ולדברי חז"ל היא עצמה הבקעה שנתקבצו בה דור הפלגה לבנות המגדל
sources.says: Malbim says, following the sages, that this is the same valley where the generation of the Tower gathered, and that the king chose it for a similar aim.

3:4.headline: Peoples, nations and tongues: three words, three groups
3:4.body: The herald calls 'peoples, nations and tongues'. Metzudat Zion says a people has a god and a law, a nation has neither, and tongues are groups set apart by language. Malbim says a people has its own ruler and a nation its own religion.

sources.quote: הם בלא אלוה ובלא תורה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the אומיא are nations without a god and without a law.

sources.quote: הם האומות שיש להם אלוה ותורה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the עממיא are nations that have a god and a law.

sources.quote: כי כל עם ועם י"ל מושל מיוחד, וכל אומה ואומה מופרדת בדת מיוחד
sources.says: Malbim says each people has its own ruler, each nation its own religion, and each tongue its own language.

3:9.headline: They did not just 'answer'; they shouted
3:9.body: ענו usually means 'they answered'. Rashi says that throughout the Bible this verb means speaking in a raised voice.

sources.quote: צָוְחוּ. כָּל עֲנִיָּה שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא לְשׁוֹן קוֹל רָם הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says they shouted, and that every 'answering' in Scripture means a raised voice.

sources.quote: הרימו קול ואמרו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they raised their voices and spoke.

3:14.headline: 'Is it true?' or 'Is my decree empty to you?'
3:14.body: The king asks הצדא. Ibn Ezra and Malbim read it as 'is it true?'. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it from the Aramaic word for waste and emptiness: 'is my decree nothing to you?'

sources.quote: שֶׁמָּא גְּזֵרוֹתַי צָדוּ וְשַׁמָּה וְדָבָר רֵיק הִיא בְּעֵינֵיכֶם
sources.says: Rashi says the king asks whether his decrees are desolate and empty in their eyes.

sources.quote: ענין שממה כי תהו ובהו (בראשית א׳:ב׳) ת״א צדיא ורקניא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means desolation, as Onkelos translates 'without form and void' with צדיא.

sources.quote: שאלם האמת הוא ככה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the king asked them whether it is true.

3:16.headline: They call him by name, without 'king'
3:16.body: The three answer the king as just 'Nebuchadnezzar'. Rashi says they meant: in taxes you are our king, but if you ask us to deny God, you are a lowly man to us.

sources.quote: אִם לִכְפּוֹר בְּהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר שְׁפַל אֲנָשִׁים בְּעֵינֵינוּ
sources.says: Rashi says they told him: for taxes you are our king, but to deny God, Nebuchadnezzar, you are the lowliest of men to us.

sources.quote: ולא קראוהו בשם מלך כאומר בדבר זה לא תמלוך עלינו
sources.says: Metzudat David says they did not call him king, as if to say that in this matter he does not rule over them.

3:18.headline: 'Even if not': they did not count on a miracle
3:18.body: The three say God can save them, 'and if not', they still will not bow. Rashi uses these words to teach that one who gives up his life to honor God must not do it expecting a miracle.

sources.quote: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בַחֲנַנְיָה מִישָׁאֵל וַעֲזַרְיָה שֶׁלֹּא מָסְרוּ עַצְמָן עַל מְנָת הַנֵּס
sources.says: Rashi says one who gives himself up expecting a miracle gets none, and that Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah did not give themselves up on that condition, citing this verse.

sources.quote: וְאִם לֹא יַחְפֹּץ לְהַצִּיל גּוּפֵינוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it means: and if God does not wish to save our bodies.

3:19.headline: The word for stoking the furnace, also heard in 'Tammuz'
3:19.body: למזא means to heat or stoke. Ibn Ezra hears it in Moses' phrase מזי רעב, 'burnt by hunger'. Rashi and Metzudat Zion say the idol Tammuz in Ezekiel is named from the same word for heating.

sources.quote: ענין הסקה ושריפה וכן מזי רעב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means heating and burning, as in 'wasted by hunger' in Deuteronomy.

sources.quote: כמו שרופי רעב מגזרת למזא לאתונא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says מזי רעב means burnt by hunger, from the same root as stoking the furnace in Daniel.

sources.quote: תַּמּוּז. לְשׁוֹן הֶיסֵּק
sources.says: Rashi says the name Tammuz means heating, as in this verse in Daniel.

3:21.headline: Thrown in wearing their fine robes
3:21.body: They were bound in their cloaks and robes. Rashi says these were their official garments, and they did not change them even when facing death. The sages learned from this not to give up one's rank even in danger.

sources.quote: מִכָּאן לָמְדוּ חֲכָמִים, שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה לֹא יְשַׁנֶּה אָדָם מִן הַשְּׂרָרָה שֶׁהֻחְזַק בָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says they wore royal garments even on trial for their lives, and the sages learned from this that one should not lower one's rank even in danger.

sources.quote: כְּמוֹ בְּדָנִיֵּאל ״בְּכַרְבְּלָתְהוֹן״
sources.says: Rashi links David being 'wrapped' in a robe to this word in Daniel.

3:25.headline: How the king knew the fourth figure was an angel
3:25.body: The king sees a fourth figure 'like a son of the gods'. Rashi says it looked like the angel the king had seen when Sennacherib's army burned, since Nebuchadnezzar was there and escaped. Metzudat Zion says angels are called 'sons of God' as members of God's household.

sources.quote: דּוֹמֶה לְמַלְאָךְ שֶׁרָאִיתִי בִּהְיוֹתִי עִם סַנְחֵרִיב
sources.says: Rashi says it looked like the angel the king saw when he was with Sennacherib and the Assyrian army was burned.

sources.quote: כן יקרא המלאך כאלו הוא מבני בית של השכינה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says an angel is called this as if it were a member of God's household.

3:26.headline: 'Come out', not 'come up': the furnace floor rose
3:26.body: A furnace is a pit, so one would expect 'come up'. The king says 'come out'. Rashi learns from this that the floor of the furnace rose to ground level, so they would not have to climb.

sources.quote: צְאוּ וּבֹאוּ, וְלֹא אָמַר לָהֶם עֲלוּ וּבֹאוּ. מִכָּאן לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁצָּף קַרְקָעִית הַכִּבְשָׁן
sources.says: Rashi says the king said 'come out' and not 'come up', which teaches that the furnace floor floated up level with the ground.

sources.quote: וחז"ל דקדקו ממ"ש פוקו ולא אמר עלו, שצף הכבשן, כי דרך הכבשן להיות בעומק
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages' reading of 'come out' rather than 'come up', since a furnace is usually sunk in the ground.

4:1.headline: The king calls himself 'green', a word for a leafy tree
4:1.body: רענן means fresh and green, a word used for trees. Metzudat David says the king borrowed tree language here because his dream will compare him to a tree.

sources.quote: ועל שבהחלום אשר יספר בענין נמשל הוא אל האילן לזה אחז בלשון שאלה מליצת שבח וטובת האילן
sources.says: Metzudat David says that since the dream likens the king to a tree, he borrowed the praise of a tree to describe himself.

sources.quote: ענין לחות ורטיבות כמו דשנים ורעננים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means moist and fresh, as in the Psalm about trees that stay full of sap.

4:5.headline: Daniel's Babylonian name carries the name of Babylon's god
4:5.body: The king says Daniel was named 'after the name of my god'. Rashi explains that Bel was the god of Babylon, and the rest of the name is a word for wisdom.

sources.quote: עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁל בָּבֶל בֵּל שְׁמָהּ, טְשַׁצַּר שֵׁם לְשׁוֹן חָכְמָה הוּא בָּאוּמּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says Babylon's idol was called Bel, and the second part of the name means wisdom in the language of the nations.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם עֲבוֹדַת כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁל בָּבֶל שֶׁקְּרוּיָה בֵּל
sources.says: Rashi says the name was given after Babylon's idol Bel, and that the name means wisdom in Aramaic.

4:8.headline: Seen from the earth's end, or branches reaching it?
4:8.body: חזותה can come from the word for seeing, so the tree could be seen from the ends of the earth. Ibn Ezra also reads it as the tree's boughs, which spread that far.

sources.quote: וחזותיה - שעיפיו וכמוהו: קרן חזות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra reads the word as its boughs, comparing the phrase קרן חזות.

sources.quote: אמר ר' ישועה: כי וחזותיה מלשון חזה שהוא נראה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra quotes Rabbi Yeshua that the word comes from seeing, meaning visible, and then questions that view.

sources.quote: ומראהו היה נראה לסוף כל הארץ
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as the tree's appearance, which could be seen at the end of the earth.

5:3.headline: The king said 'the palace'; the servants said 'the house of God'
5:3.body: In verse 2 the king asks for vessels from 'the palace in Jerusalem'. In verse 3 they come from 'the house of God'. Malbim says the king would not call it God's house, but his servants still knew whose house it was.

sources.quote: שלא אמר להביא הכלים מן ההיכל של בית אלהים כמ"ש בפסוק שאח"ז, כי לא רצה לקראו בשם אלהים כלל
sources.says: Malbim says the king did not say 'house of God' as the next verse does, because he refused to call it by God's name at all.

sources.quote: אמנם שריו ועבדיו, החזיקו אותו שהוא בית אלהים וידעו שה' שוכן שם
sources.says: Malbim says his officers and servants still held it to be God's house and knew God dwelt there.

5:7.headline: A third of the kingdom, or third in rank?
5:7.body: The reward is to rule as תלתי in the kingdom. Rashi reads it as ruling one third of the kingdom. Malbim brings both views: a third of the land, or third in rank.

sources.quote: בִּשְׁלִישׁ הַמַּלְכוּת יִמְשׁוֹל
sources.says: Rashi says he will rule a third of the kingdom.

sources.quote: י"מ בשליש המלכות ימשול וי"א שיהיה שלישי למלך
sources.says: Malbim says some read it as ruling a third of the kingdom, and others as being third after the king.

5:25.headline: Broken, and given to Persia
5:25.body: פרסין means broken pieces. Daniel reads it two ways at once: the kingdom is broken, and it is given to Persia, פרס. Rashi and Ibn Ezra point out both senses.

sources.quote: ״וּפַרְסִין״ מַשְׁמַע שְׁנֵי פְרָסִין
sources.says: Rashi says the plural means two פרס: your kingdom is broken, and it is given to Media and Persia.

sources.quote: פרס האחד, שהוא פריסת שבירת מלכותו וכריתותם. ופרס השני, מגזרת מדי ופרס
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the first פרס is the breaking of his kingdom and the second is Persia.

6:1.headline: The king's age points back to Babylon entering the Temple
6:1.body: Rashi asks why the verse bothers to count Darius's years. He answers that Darius, Nebuchadnezzar's enemy, was born on the very day Nebuchadnezzar entered the Temple.

sources.quote: לָמָּה מָנָה שְׁנוֹתָיו? לוֹמַר לְךָ: בְּיוֹם שֶׁנִּכְנַס נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר לַהֵיכָל
sources.says: Rashi says the age is given to teach that Darius was born on the day Nebuchadnezzar entered the Temple.

sources.quote: להגיד שנולד ביום שנכנס נבוכדנצר להיכל
sources.says: Malbim brings the same reading from the sages, and adds that being old, Darius could not run the kingdom alone.

6:11.headline: Praying is not the same as asking, says Malbim
6:11.body: The king's ban was on asking (בעו) anything of a god or a man. Malbim says Daniel's daily prayer and thanks (מצלא ומודא) were a different act, so the ban did not cover them.

sources.quote: והבדל גדול יש בין מתפלל ובין מבקש
sources.says: Malbim says there is a big difference between praying and asking, and the decree banned only asking.

6:12.headline: The accusers switch the word from praying to asking
6:12.body: Verse 11 says Daniel prayed and gave thanks. Here his accusers find him 'asking', and Malbim says the word changes because they wanted his prayer to fit the king's ban on requests.

sources.quote: שינה הלשון שמצאו אותו מבקש
sources.says: Malbim says the verse changes the word to 'asking' because the accusers meant to claim he made a private request.

6:12.headline: A noisy crowd bursting in, or men feeling around for him
6:12.body: Metzudat Zion reads הרגשו as gathering in a noisy crowd, as in Psalm 2, 'why do the nations rage'. Rashi reads it as feeling around and seizing Daniel.

sources.quote: ענין קבוץ כי בקבוץ עם רב נשמע קול המיה ורגישה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means gathering, because a big crowd makes noise, as in 'why do the nations rage'.

sources.quote: הִרְגִּישׁוּ. מִשְׁמְשׁוּ וְתָפְשׁוּ
sources.says: Rashi glosses it as 'they felt around and seized'.

6:15.headline: A one-time verb for the king's struggle to save Daniel
6:15.body: Ibn Ezra notes that משתדר has no partner word anywhere and reads it as planning with all his strength. Metzudat Zion links it to השתדל, 'make an effort', in the sages' Hebrew.

sources.quote: משתדר. אין לו חבר ופירושו כמו מחשב בכל יכולתו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner, and means thinking with all his ability.

sources.quote: ענין ספק והשתדלות בדרז״ל השתדל להיות איש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means making an effort, like השתדל in the sages' words 'try to be a man'.

6:18.headline: No stones in Babylon, so where did this one come from?
6:18.body: Rashi says Babylon had no stone, only brick, as Genesis 11 shows. So he says angels brought this one from the land of Israel for the moment.

sources.quote: לָמַדְנוּ שֶׁאֵין אֶבֶן בְּבָבֶל, וּלְפִי שָׁעָה הֱבִיאוּהָ מַלְאָכִים מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says there is no stone in Babylon, so angels brought this stone from the land of Israel.

6:23.headline: An angel, or any force that carries out God's will?
6:23.body: Maimonides says מלאך simply means a messenger, so anything that carries out a command is one. He cites this verse to show that even what animals do can be credited to an angel.

sources.quote: ואם כן כל מבצע ציווי הוא מלאך
sources.says: Maimonides says 'angel' means a messenger, so whatever carries out a command is an angel, and he cites this verse about the lions.

7:1.headline: Daniel calls his vision a 'dream'
7:1.body: Maimonides notes that Daniel calls his visions dreams even when an angel speaks to him. He takes this as a level below full prophecy, which is why Daniel sits among the Writings, not the Prophets. Malbim notes the verse says Daniel 'saw' a dream, marking it as prophetic.

sources.quote: וכן אתה מוצא את דניאל מדבר עליהם כעל חלומות
sources.says: Maimonides says Daniel speaks of his visions as dreams, a lower level than full prophecy, and that this is why his book was placed among the Writings.

sources.quote: ולא אמר חלם חלם, כמ"ש למעלה בנבוכדנצר להורות שהיה חלום נבואיי
sources.says: Malbim says the verse avoids 'dreamed a dream', as said of Nebuchadnezzar, to show this was a prophetic dream.

7:4.headline: A 'human' heart, or a weak one?
7:4.body: The lion is given a human heart. Rashi hears frailty in אנש, as in 'let the nations know they are mortal'. Metzudat David says a human heart is simply not as brave as a lion's.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן חֲלָשׁוּת, כְּמוֹ ״יֵדְעוּ גוֹיִם אֱנוֹשׁ הֵמָּה״
sources.says: Rashi says the word means weakness, as in the Psalm 'let the nations know they are but mortal'.

sources.quote: ונתן לה לבב בן אדם שאין לו לב אמיץ כלב האריה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it was given a human heart, which is not as bold as a lion's heart.

7:5.headline: A bear spelled so that it also hints at a wolf
7:5.body: The second beast is like a bear, דב. Rashi notes the spelling without a vav, which recalls דיבא, Aramaic for wolf. Persia is also called a wolf by Jeremiah.

sources.quote: לְדֹב כְּתִיב, כְּמוֹ ״דִּיבָא״ תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁל זְאֵב
sources.says: Rashi says the word is written so it can read like דיבא, the Aramaic for wolf, since Persia is also called a wolf in Jeremiah.

sources.quote: שֶׁאוֹכְלִים וְשׁוֹתִים כַּדֹּב וּמְסֻרְבָּלִים בְּבָשָׂר כַּדֹּב
sources.says: Rashi says the bear stands for Persia, whose people eat and drink like a bear and are heavy with flesh like a bear.

7:5.headline: Three ribs in the bear's mouth: three lands, or three kings?
7:5.body: The bear holds three ribs between its teeth. Rashi brings the sages: three lands Persia kept swallowing and spitting out. Rashi's own view is three Persian kings. Malbim says three kingdoms it seized.

sources.quote: שָׁלֹשׁ מְדִינוֹת הָיוּ תָּמִיד מוֹרְדוֹת בָּהּ וּמַשְׁלִימוֹת עִמָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi brings the sages that these are three lands that kept rebelling and making peace, and then gives his own view: three kings of Persia, Cyrus, Ahasuerus and Darius.

sources.quote: שתפס שלש מלכיות שהוא מלכות בבל ומלכות אשור ומלכות מדי ופרס
sources.says: Malbim says the ribs are three kingdoms it seized: Babylon, Assyria, and Media-Persia.

7:6.headline: A leopard, because its decrees were 'spotted'
7:6.body: The third beast is a leopard, נמר. Rashi and Metzudat David hear the word for spotted: this kingdom's decrees against Israel were varied, each one different, like a leopard's spots.

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם שֶׁהָיְתָה גּוֹזֶרֶת גְּזֵרוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מְנֻמָּרוֹת וּמְשֻׁנּוֹת זוֹ מִזּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is called a leopard because it issued decrees against Israel that were spotted and different from one another.

sources.quote: ע״ש שגזרו גזרות על ישראל משונות זה מזה כנמר הזה המנומר בחברבורות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it stands for Greece, whose decrees on Israel were all different, like a leopard's spots.

7:7.headline: Why the fourth beast came on a separate night
7:7.body: The verse mentions the night again before the fourth beast. Rashi says Daniel saw it on a second night, because this beast weighs as much as the other three together. Malbim says the long night stands for a long, dark exile.

sources.quote: הַשָּׁלֹשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת רָאָה בְּלַיְלָה אַחַת, וְזוֹ בְּלַיְלָה אַחֶרֶת
sources.says: Rashi says Daniel saw the first three beasts on one night and this one on another, because it equals all three.

sources.quote: כי בו ראה לילה ארוכה וגלות חשוך מאד
sources.says: Malbim says in this beast Daniel saw a long night, a very dark exile.

7:9.headline: Thrones set up, or thrones thrown down?
7:9.body: רמיו usually means 'were cast'. Rashi reads it as thrones placed for judgment. Malbim brings the midrash: these are the thrones of the nations, thrown down.

sources.quote: כִּסְאוֹת הוּטְלוּ וְנִתְקְנוּ לֵישֵׁב בְּמִשְׁפָּט
sources.says: Rashi says thrones were set in place for judgment, one for justice and one for kindness to Israel.

sources.quote: עד די כרסון יתיב אין כתיב כאן אלא רמיו
sources.says: Malbim brings Tanchuma: the verse does not say the thrones were set but that they were cast, meaning the thrones of the nations will be overturned.

7:9.headline: Who is the 'Ancient of Days'?
7:9.body: עתיק יומין can mean someone old in years. Malbim says it is God, who is beyond time. Metzudat David says God appears as an old man to show mercy. Ibn Ezra reads it as the angel Michael.

sources.quote: שהוא נעתק מן הימים והזמן
sources.says: Malbim says it means God, who is removed from days and time.

sources.quote: וזהו כי ראה את השכינה בדמות זקן להורות שהוא מלא רחמים
sources.says: Metzudat David says Daniel saw God's presence as an old man to show that God is full of mercy.

sources.quote: וזה יהיה בעמוד מיכאל שר הגדול כאשר יפרש והוא עתיק יומין
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says this will happen when Michael the great prince stands up, and that Michael is the one called עתיק יומין.

7:9.headline: Hair like clean wool: who is being cleaned?
7:9.body: The judge's hair is like clean wool, נקא. Rashi says God clears away the nations' merits by paying them back in this world. Metzudat David says God cleans Israel of its sins.

sources.quote: מְנַקֶּה עַצְמוֹ מִזְּכֻיּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת לְפָנָיו
sources.says: Rashi says God clears himself of the merits the idol worshippers have, paying their full reward in this world.

sources.quote: ושער ראשה כעמר נקי לרמז שינקה אותם מפשעם
sources.says: Metzudat David says the clean wool hints that God will clean his people of their sins.

7:10.headline: A river of fire, or a light of fire?
7:10.body: נהר די נור is usually read as a river of fire flowing out. Ibn Ezra prefers to read it as נהור, a light of fire.

sources.quote: יש אומרים: נהור אש והוא הנכון בעיני
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says some read it as a light of fire, and he thinks that is right.

sources.quote: נחל של אש היה נמשך ויוצא מלפניו
sources.says: Metzudat David reads it as a stream of fire flowing out before God.

7:13.headline: One 'like a son of man': the Messiah, or Israel?
7:13.body: A figure like a human comes with the clouds. Rashi says it is the Messiah, and also that Israel is pictured as a human, while the nations are beasts. Ibn Ezra says it is the holy people, Israel.

sources.quote: כְּבַר אֱנָשׁ אָתֵה. הוּא מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ
sources.says: Rashi says the one like a son of man is the King Messiah.

sources.quote: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל דִּימָּה כְּבֶן אָדָם עַל שֶׁהֵם עֲנְוְתָנִים וּתְמִימִים
sources.says: Rashi says the nations are pictured as beasts and Israel as a human, because Israel is humble and wholehearted.

sources.quote: ויאמר רבי ישועה: כי זה כבר אנש הוא המשיח. ונכון דבר רק הוא עם הקדש שהם ישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra quotes Rabbi Yeshua that it is the Messiah, and says it is rather the holy people, Israel.

7:15.headline: A one-time word for Daniel's distress
7:15.body: אתכרית appears nowhere else. Rashi reads it from כרה, to dig: Daniel's spirit was torn from its deep place. Malbim reads it from the Aramaic for 'short of spirit', meaning distress.

sources.quote: ומלת אתכרית – אין לה ריע
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner anywhere else.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן ״כִּי יִכְרֶה״ (שמות כב:לג), וְלָשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי וְעִבְרִי שָׁוִין בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it comes from the verb to dig, the same in Aramaic and Hebrew: the spirit was pulled from its deep place.

sources.quote: תרגום של קוצר רוח דכריה רוחיה
sources.says: Malbim says it is the Aramaic used to translate 'shortness of spirit': my spirit grew short.

7:15.headline: The body is the spirit's sheath
7:15.body: נדנה is a sheath, as for a sword. Daniel says his spirit was troubled inside its sheath. Rashi and Ibn Ezra explain the sheath as the body, which holds the spirit like a sword.

sources.quote: בְּתוֹךְ תִּיקָה, נַרְתֵּק שֶׁלּוֹ, כְּלוֹמַר: נִבְהֲלָה רוּחִי בְּתוֹךְ הַגּוּף
sources.says: Rashi says it means inside its case, that is, my spirit was shaken inside my body.

sources.quote: ענין תיק ונרתק כמו וישב חרבו אל נדנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a case, as in 'he returned his sword to its sheath'.

sources.quote: כי הגוף לרוח כנדן והעד איתכרית רוחי
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the body is to the spirit like a sheath, and brings this verse in Daniel as proof.

7:25.headline: 'A time, times and half a time': how long?
7:25.body: Israel will suffer for a time, times and half a time. Rashi says this end date was hidden on purpose, and every earlier reckoning of it has passed. Metzudat David reads it as two and a half years. Malbim reads each 'time' as hundreds of years.

sources.quote: וּדְרָשׁוּהוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנִים אִישׁ לְפִי דַעְתּוֹ, וְכָלוּ הַקִּצִּים
sources.says: Rashi says this is a sealed end; the earlier sages each worked it out their own way, and those dates have passed.

sources.quote: ר״ל שתי שנים וחצי שנה יהיו מסורים בידו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means two and a half years.

sources.quote: והוא או ארבע מאות שנה מועד גלות מצרים, או ת"י שנה זמן שעמד מקדש ראשון
sources.says: Malbim says a 'time' is a known span: either the 400 years of Egypt or the 410 years the First Temple stood.

8:1.headline: A 'vision' and a 'sight' are one thing, says Maimonides
8:1.body: Daniel calls this a חזון, a vision. Maimonides says חזון comes from חזה and מראה from ראה, and both mean seeing. Prophecy comes in only two ways, a vision or a dream, with levels within each.

sources.quote: ול"חזה" ו"ראה" יש משמעות אחת
sources.says: Maimonides says the verbs חזה and ראה have one meaning.

sources.quote: אין דרך שלישית מלבד שתי הדרכים שדיברה עליהם התורה במפורש
sources.says: Maimonides says there is no third way of prophecy beside the two the Torah names, a vision and a dream.

8:11.headline: The 'prince of the host': God, the angel Michael, or a priest?
8:11.body: Rashi says the horn raised itself against God, prince of Israel's host. Ibn Ezra says the prince is the angel Michael. Malbim reads it as Mattathias the priest and his Maccabee sons, who grew strong and won.

sources.quote: שַׂר הַצָּבָא כְּלַפֵּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא חֵרֵף
sources.says: Rashi says the 'prince of the host' means he blasphemed against God.

sources.quote: ועד צבא השמים שר הצבא שהוא מיכאל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the prince of the host is Michael.

sources.quote: שהוא מתתיהו הכהן ובניו המכביים
sources.says: Malbim says the prince of the host is Mattathias the priest and his sons the Maccabees.

8:11.headline: The daily offering was 'lifted': taken away, or raised again?
8:11.body: The word is written הרים and read הורם, and it can mean lifted away or lifted high. Rashi reads that the daily offering was stopped. Malbim reads the opposite: through the Maccabees, the offering the Greeks had stopped was raised up again.

sources.quote: וְעַל יְדֵי גְדוּדָיו וְחֵילוֹתָיו שֶׁשָּׁלַח לִירוּשָׁלַיִם בָּטֵל הַתָּמִיד
sources.says: Rashi says that through the troops he sent to Jerusalem the daily offering was stopped.

sources.quote: הורם. ל׳ הרמה וסלוק
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means lifting and removal.

sources.quote: שהתמיד שהיה בטל עד הנה על ידי היונים נתרומם
sources.says: Malbim says the daily offering, stopped until then by the Greeks, was raised up again.

8:13.headline: The 'desolating sin' is an idol as silent as stone
8:13.body: שמם usually means desolate. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it here as mute and still. The 'silent sin' is the idol set up in place of the daily offering, as speechless as a stone.

sources.quote: שׁוֹמֵם. לְשׁוֹן אִלֵּם וּמְשֻׁתָּק
sources.says: Rashi says שומם means mute and silenced.

sources.quote: פֶּשַׁע שֹׁמֵם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מֵעוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים שֶׁהִיא כְּאֶבֶן דּוֹמֵם
sources.says: Rashi says the 'silent sin' is idol worship, which is like a mute stone.

sources.quote: שומם. משותק כמו משמים בתוכם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means silenced, as in Ezekiel sitting 'stunned among them'.

8:16.headline: A man's voice, with no one to be seen
8:16.body: Daniel hears קול אדם, a man's voice, from between the banks of the Ulai. Maimonides lists this as one kind of prophecy: the prophet sees no figure and only hears speech. Malbim says the speaker was the hidden angel, and cites a midrash that reads the 'man' as God.

sources.quote: ויש שהנביא אינו רואה אף צורה, אלא הוא שומע דיבור בלבד הקורא לו במראה הנבואה
sources.says: Maimonides says that sometimes the prophet sees no form at all and only hears speech calling to him in the prophetic vision.

sources.quote: ואותו לא ראה כי הוא פלמוני ונעלם רק שמע קולו מבין הנהר מרחוק
sources.says: Malbim says Daniel did not see the speaker, the hidden one, but only heard his voice from the river, far off.

sources.quote: גדול כחם של נביאים שמדמין הצורה ליוצרה שנאמר ואשמע קול אדם בין אולי
sources.says: Malbim cites the midrash: great is the power of the prophets, who liken the form to its Maker, as it says 'I heard a man's voice'.

8:16.headline: 'This one': a plain pointer, or a mark of honor?
8:16.body: Gabriel is told to explain the vision להלז, to this one. Metzudat Zion reads it simply as 'this'. Rashi says הלז is a word of respect, used for someone of striking appearance.

sources.quote: להלז. להזה כמו השונמית הלז
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'to this one', as in 'that Shunammite'.

sources.quote: לְהַלָּז. לְשׁוֹן חֲשִׁיבוּת
sources.says: Rashi says it is a term of importance.

sources.quote: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ׳הַלָּז׳ בַּעַל צוּרָה הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says wherever הלז is said, the person is of fine appearance.

8:19.headline: An 'appointed time' cannot slip like ordinary time
8:19.body: Gabriel first says לעת קץ, at the time of the end, then למועד קץ, at the appointed time. Malbim says עת is time as nature runs, which God may change, but a מועד is a time set by a promise, and a good promise with a date cannot be changed.

sources.quote: ויש הבדל בין עת ובין מועד, שהעת הוא העת הטבעי, שהוא מעצמו, והמועד הוא העת המיועד על ידי מי שיעדו
sources.says: Malbim says עת is natural time, which comes by itself, while מועד is a time set by the one who appointed it.

sources.quote: אבל היעוד הטוב שיעד בנבואה והגביל הזמן
sources.says: Malbim says a good promise made in prophecy with a fixed time cannot be changed.

8:24.headline: Strong 'not by his strength': through smooth talk, or Israel's sins?
8:24.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say the king grows strong through smooth talk and tricks, not might. Ibn Ezra says his power comes only because God used him to punish Israel for their sins.

sources.quote: וְלֹא בִּגְבוּרָה כִּי אִם בַּחֲלַקְלַקּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it is not by might but by smooth flattery.

sources.quote: ולא בעבור רוב כוחו כ״א בחלקלקות אמריו ותחבולות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is not through great strength but through smooth words and schemes.

sources.quote: ועצם כחו ולא בכחו - רק בעבור חטאת ישראל ליסרם השם
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says his strength comes only because of Israel's sin, so that God could discipline them.

8:25.headline: Broken 'with no hand': by a gnat, or by a fall?
8:25.body: The king will be broken באפס יד, with no hand against him. Rashi, following the Talmud, says Titus was killed by a tiny gnat that entered his nose. Ibn Ezra, who reads the king as Antiochus, says he fell from a roof and died.

sources.quote: וּבְאֵין כֹּחַ יִשָּׁבֵר עַל יְדֵי יַתּוּשׁ חַלָּשׁ שֶׁבַּבְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁנִּכְנַס בְּחוֹטְמוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says he will be broken without force, by a gnat, the weakest creature, that entered his nose.

sources.quote: מבלי יד אדם ימות
sources.says: Metzudat David says he will die with no human hand.

sources.quote: כי ידוע הוא אנטיוכוס נפל מן הגג ונשבר ומת
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is known that Antiochus fell from a roof, broke, and died.

8:27.headline: Not 'I became' but 'I was broken'
8:27.body: נהייתי looks like 'I became', from the verb 'to be'. Rashi and the Metzudot read it as 'I was broken', as in chapter 2 where Nebuchadnezzar's sleep was broken. Daniel was crushed and sick for days.

sources.quote: נִהְיֵיתִי. לְשׁוֹן הֹוֶה וְשֶׁבֶר
sources.says: Rashi says נהייתי means calamity and breaking.

sources.quote: נהייתי. נשברתי וכן ושנתו נהיתה עליו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'I was broken', as in 'his sleep was broken from him'.

sources.quote: נשברתי ונעשיתי חולה כמה ימים מרוב החרדה
sources.says: Metzudat David says Daniel was broken and became sick for some days from great fear.

9:2.headline: 'In the books', or 'in the numbers'?
9:2.body: ספרים usually means books. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it here as reckonings: Daniel was counting the years Jeremiah foretold. Malbim asks why it says 'books' when Jeremiah is one book, and says Daniel found a second book with another wording.

sources.quote: בִּינוֹתִי בַסְּפָרִים. נִסְתַּכַּלְתִּי בַחֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says 'I understood in the books' means I looked into the calculations.

sources.quote: בספרים. מלשון מספר וחשבון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from counting and reckoning.

sources.quote: למה אמר ספרים והוא ספר אחד
sources.says: Malbim asks why it says 'books' when it is one book.

sources.quote: ומצא בספר אחד שהיה כתוב בו
sources.says: Malbim says Daniel found another book in which it was written differently.

9:4.headline: Great and awesome, but Daniel leaves out 'mighty'
9:4.body: Moses called God great, mighty and awesome. Daniel says only great and awesome. Rashi explains why: with foreigners ruling God's children, Daniel asked, where is His might?

sources.quote: הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל וְהַנּוֹרָא. וְלֹא אָמַר גִּבּוֹר
sources.says: Rashi notes Daniel said 'great and awesome' but did not say 'mighty'.

sources.quote: עוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים מִשְׁתַּעְבְּדִים בְּבָנָיו וְאַיֵּה גְּבוּרוֹתָיו
sources.says: Rashi gives his reason: idol worshippers enslave God's children, so where is His might?

9:14.headline: God hurried the exile, and the Sages call that a kindness
9:14.body: וישקד means God hurried to bring the harm. Rashi brings the Sages: the haste was itself kindness. God sent the exile two years before the number hidden in ונושנתם, 852, so the threat 'you will surely perish' would not come true.

sources.quote: וישקד. ענין מהירות כמו כי שוקד אני
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word means haste, as in 'for I hasten' in Jeremiah.

sources.quote: צַדִּיק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וּצְדָקָה הִיא עָלֵינוּ, שֶׁמִּהֵר וְהִקְדִּים שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
sources.says: Rashi cites the Sages: God is righteous and it was a kindness to us that He hurried and came two years early.

sources.quote: ״וְנוֹשַׁנְתֶּם״ בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא: שְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם
sources.says: Rashi says the letters of ונושנתם add up to 852.

9:18.headline: God's 'eyes' mean knowing, not seeing
9:18.body: Daniel asks God to open His eyes and see the ruin. Maimonides says that when the Bible joins seeing to God's eyes, it means knowing with the mind, not seeing with the senses. Every sense is acted on, and God acts but is never acted on.

sources.quote: משמעות הדבר הזה כולו היא השגה שכלית ולא השגה חושית
sources.says: Maimonides says the meaning of all this is grasping with the mind, not with the senses.

sources.quote: שהרי כל תחושה היא היפעלות והתרשמות
sources.says: He says every sensing is being acted on and receiving an impression.

sources.quote: והוא יתעלה פועל ולא נפעל
sources.says: He says God acts and is not acted on.

9:21.headline: 'The man Gabriel': an angel seen only in a vision
9:21.body: Daniel calls the angel Gabriel 'the man'. Maimonides says all of this happened inside a prophetic vision. No one sees an angel or hears one speak except in a vision or a prophetic dream.

sources.quote: כל זה במראה הנבואה
sources.says: Maimonides says that all of Daniel's account of the man Gabriel took place in a prophetic vision.

sources.quote: אל יעלה על דעתך בשום אופן שיש ראיית מלאך או שמיעת דיבור מלאך אלא במראה הנבואה או בחלום שלנבואה
sources.says: He says never to think an angel is seen or heard except in a prophetic vision or a prophetic dream.

9:21.headline: Flying, or worn out from the flight?
9:21.body: מעף ביעף sounds like flying twice over. Rashi reads both words as flight. Ibn Ezra reads ביעף from יעף, tired: Gabriel was weary from the speed. Malbim brings the Sages: Gabriel arrives in two flights.

sources.quote: הָיָה מוּעָף אֵלַי בִּפְרִיחָה וּבְטִיסָה
sources.says: Rashi says Gabriel came flying to him, in flight and soaring.

sources.quote: וטעם ביעף – כי הוא יעף מרוב המרוצה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says ביעף means he was tired from all the rushing.

sources.quote: וחז"ל אמרו שעף בשתי עפיפות כי גבריאל בשתים
sources.says: Malbim cites the Sages that he flew in two flights, since Gabriel arrives in two.

9:23.headline: 'You are delights': Daniel is a man much loved
9:23.body: Gabriel tells Daniel חמודות אתה, word for word 'you are delights'. Ibn Ezra says the word 'man' is left out: a man of delights, the way 'I am prayer' means a man of prayer. Rashi says Daniel is dear to God.

sources.quote: כי חמודות אתה - בחסרון איש, כמו: ואני תפילה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word 'man' is missing, as in 'and I am prayer'.

sources.quote: דִּבְרֵי חֶמֶד יֵשׁ לְךָ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says Daniel has things of delight before God.

sources.quote: על שאתה בעל מעלות חמודות
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is because Daniel has precious qualities.

9:24.headline: Seventy 'sevens': weeks of years, not of days
9:24.body: The verse says שבעים שבעים, 'seventy sevens'. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read each 'seven' as a cycle of seven years, 490 years in all. Malbim says the number fits the cause of the exile: Israel had not kept the seventh-year rest.

sources.quote: שבועים. שמטות משבע שנים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says these 'weeks' are seven-year cycles.

sources.quote: וּמִנְיַן שָׁבוּעִים אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה
sources.says: Rashi says the count of weeks is 490 years.

sources.quote: הם שבעים שמטות, כי השבעים שנה היו בעון השמטות
sources.says: Malbim says they are seventy seven-year cycles, since the seventy years of exile came for the sin of not keeping the seventh year.

9:24.headline: Sealing vision and prophet: fulfilled, or shut off?
9:24.body: To 'seal' can mean to finish or to close. Metzudat Zion says it means completing, the way a writer signs at the end. Metzudat David reads it as every promise of the prophets coming true. Ibn Ezra reads it as prophecy stopping, which he calls bad news.

sources.quote: כי דרך לרשום כ״א שמו אחר גמר הכתב
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means completion, since each person signs his name after finishing a document.

sources.quote: להתקיים כל היעודים והבשורות אשר נבאו כל הנביאים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means all the promises and good news of all the prophets will be fulfilled.

sources.quote: ולחתום חזון ונביא - שיפסקו הנביאים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says sealing vision and prophet means the prophets will stop.

sources.quote: רק ולחתום חזון ונביא איננו לשבח
sources.says: He says sealing vision and prophet is not said as praise.

9:25.headline: 'Anointed' here means a ruler, not the Messiah
9:25.body: משיח means anointed. Rashi says it here means Cyrus, whom Isaiah calls God's anointed, and that משיח just means a prince or great man. Malbim reads it as Israel's own anointed high priest or king. Ibn Ezra rejects the Cyrus reading.

sources.quote: עַד בֹּא כֹּרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ פָּרַס
sources.says: Rashi says the 'anointed prince' is Cyrus, king of Persia.

sources.quote: מָשִׁיחַ. אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן שַׂר וְגָדוֹל
sources.says: Rashi says משיח here only means a prince and great man.

sources.quote: ולמשוח. ענין גדולה כמו למשיחי לכורש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says anointing means greatness, as in 'to His anointed, to Cyrus'.

sources.quote: שהיה להם משיח, כ"ג שנמשח בשמן או נשיא ומלך שנקראו משיח
sources.says: Malbim says they had an anointed one: a high priest anointed with oil, or a prince or king, who were called משיח.

sources.quote: וראייתו, כי כורש הוא משיח איננו נכונה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the proof that Cyrus is the משיח here is not correct.

9:27.headline: 'The many' are the nobles
9:27.body: לרבים usually means 'with the many'. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as 'with the great ones', the officials, as in 'all the king's nobles' in Jeremiah. Rashi says the pact was made with Israel's leaders.

sources.quote: לָרַבִּים לַשָּׂרִים, כְּמוֹ ״וְכָל רַבֵּי הַמֶּלֶךְ״
sources.says: Rashi says 'the many' are the officials, as in 'all the king's nobles'.

sources.quote: לרבים. לשרים כמו ורבי המלך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means the officials, as in 'the king's nobles'.

sources.quote: טִיטוּס בְּרִית לְשָׂרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
sources.says: Rashi says Titus made a pact with Israel's officials.

9:27.headline: The idol that 'desolates': mute as stone, or appalling
9:27.body: משמם is often read as 'desolating'. Rashi and Metzudat Zion read it as silent and mute: an idol that cannot speak, like a stone. Ibn Ezra reads it as appalling: it shocks every Israelite who sees it or hears of it.

sources.quote: משומם. משותק ונאלם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means silenced and mute.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִיא נֶאֱלֶמֶת כְּאֶבֶן דּוֹמֵם
sources.says: Rashi says the idol is mute like a silent stone.

sources.quote: והטעם שהוא משומם כל רואו וכל שמעו מישראל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it appalls every Israelite who sees it or hears of it.
